originalTitle: Colombia earthquake live updates: more than 100 dead and buildings collapsed after 7.4-magnitude quake
summary: More than a dozen buildings collapsed in aftermath of earthquake, which has also prompted evacuations
content: The US has promised $15.5m to Colombia for earthquake relief and said it is ready to support the new president’s response. The state department said on social media the funding would go to “emergency shelter, food, protection and earthquake assessments”. The post said: We are united in prayer with the Colombian people and stand ready to support President [Abelardo De La ‌Espriella] and his government as they assess the needs on the ground. At the weekend the state department announced the Trump administration would provide $1bn in security assistance to the ⁠government of the new rightwing ‌president, who used his inaugural speech to pledge a fight against drug trafficking as well as austerity measures to restore economic confidence. Further to the last post: Mauricio Andrade, a firefighter in Colombia’s third-largest city of Cali, said his team had rescued two adult women and two children from a collapsed building. As he spoke, his team was preparing to rescue more people from the rubble. “They are alive,” he told Reuters. “We are making space so we can free them and get them out.” Juan Carlos Osorio told Caracol Television that the collapse of one building “sounded like a bomb”, as he helped remove debris from a collapsed structure in Cali. All of us neighbours are working together, forming human chains. We need heavy equipment. There are many people trapped. Reports from Choco, near the epicentre of the quake, have been slowed by communications outages, with some areas still lacking mobile phone service hours after the earthquake. ‌ Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba said 12 people had been killed and 84 injured in the largely rural area, as mentioned. The quake’s heaviest casualties appeared to be concentrated in Risaralda, part of Colombia’s coffee-growing region. Pereira, the department’s capital, suffered extensive damage, with rescue workers continuing to search collapsed buildings for survivors. A four-story building crumbled in Pereira during the quake, according to Reuters-verified video, while footage from Manizales showed one of the side towers of the city’s landmark neo-Gothic cathedral collapsing and scattering debris onto nearby streets. Reuters footage showed rescue workers, police and volunteers shovelling debris by hand and loading rubble into trucks as they searched for trapped survivors. ‌Other footage showed damage to residential towers and emergency-service facilities, with debris crashing onto ambulances parked below. Colombia’s Pacific region around the epicentre of the earthquake lies along the Ring of Fire, the line of seismic faults encircling the Pacific Ocean where most of the world’s quakes occur. The Pacific, particularly the Choco region where the quake hit, is one of Colombia’s poorest and is nestled in dense jungle. Much of the region is reachable only by boat or plane, which may pose a problem for authorities in assessing the wider toll, as the AP reports. Northwestern University seismologist Suzan van der Lee said the quake’s powerful magnitude, inland location and strike-slip motion may have amplified damage in populated valleys despite its considerable depth. “This one was far below the crust, and in ‌theory it shouldn’t cause as much shaking,” she said, quoted by Reuters. “At this magnitude, it did actually cause a lot of shaking.” The Colombia earthquake has left many people trapped under the debris of damaged buildings as their loved ones and rescue workers search through the rubble. Search teams and civilians picked through the remains of destroyed buildings in the country’s third-largest city, Cali, passing large pieces of concrete and other rubble down a long line of volunteers. “Our building has basically been left in ruins, and the building next to ours? Completely collapsed,” said Álvaro López, who cradled his dog as he watched the search. The desperate scene recalled the searches still ongoing in neighbouring Venezuela weeks after that country was devastated by back-to-back quakes in June, the Associated Press reports. Besides Cali, the quake-ravaged cities across western Colombia including Pereira, Quibdo and Manizales and was felt in neighboring Ecuador and Panama. At least 111 have died and 87 people injured after dozens of buildings collapsed following a 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck western Colombia on Monday morning – the largest to hit the country so far this century. After declaring a state of national disaster, Colombia’s new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said in an address to the nation that his government had deployed all of its capabilities “to protect lives, assist affected ‌communities and deliver aid wherever it is needed”. “The first priority is rescuing the people trapped under the rubble,” he said after around 1,600 buildings had been damaged, including at least 61 that completely collapsed. The president declared an emergency to expedite funding for the quake recovery while saying he would visit the disaster zone. “We aren’t going to leave people alone. They are in our hearts and we are going to tend to people with our full determination,” he said. The quake hit the remote Chocó region around 7.30am local time on Monday morning and was felt as far as the capital Bogotá (250 miles away), as well as neighbouring countries Ecuador, Venezuela and Panama. The epicentre was in San Jose Del Palmar, a community of about 4,800 people, and the initial quake was followed by two 2.8 and 4.8 magnitude aftershocks. Local officials confirmed deaths across several regions, including the coffee region of Risaralda and in Valle del Cauca, while rescue teams race to free people trapped under debris of collapsed buildings. Among the worst-hit areas was the city of Pereira, where at least 40 people have been killed, according to the mayor. chineseTitle: 哥伦比亚地震实时更新：7.4级地震造成100多人死亡、建筑物倒塌
chineseSummary: 地震后十几栋建筑物倒塌，也促使人们疏散
chineseContent: 美国已承诺向哥伦比亚提供1550万美元用于抗震救灾，并表示已准备好支持新总统的应对措施。美国国务院在社交媒体上表示，这笔资金将用于“紧急避难所、食品、保护和地震评估”。帖子称：我们与哥伦比亚人民团结一致祈祷，并随时准备支持总统[阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉]和他的政府评估当地的需求。周末，国务院宣布特朗普政府将向新右翼总统的政府提供 10 亿美元的安全援助，新总统在就职演说中承诺打击贩毒，并采取紧缩措施恢复经济信心。继上一篇文章之后：哥伦比亚第三大城市卡利的消防员毛里西奥·安德拉德表示，他的团队从倒塌的建筑物中救出了两名成年妇女和两名儿童。在他讲话时，他的团队正准备从废墟中营救更多人。 “他们还活着，”他告诉路透社。 “我们正在腾出空间，这样我们就可以释放他们并把他们救出来。”胡安·卡洛斯·奥索里奥 (Juan Carlos Osorio) 告诉卡拉科尔电视台，一栋建筑的倒塌“听起来像炸弹”，因为他帮助清除了卡利一栋倒塌建筑的残骸。我们所有的邻居正在共同努力，形成人链。我们需要重型设备。有很多人被困。来自震中附近的乔科的报告因通信中断而减慢，一些地区在地震发生后数小时内仍然缺乏移动电话服务。 ‌ 如前所述，州长努比亚·卡罗莱纳·科尔多瓦 (Nubia Carolina Cordoba) 表示，该地区大部分农村地区已造成 12 人死亡、84 人受伤。地震中伤亡最严重的地区似乎集中在哥伦比亚咖啡种植区的里萨拉尔达。每
